_comment: Published radii to compare against, by container and metric. These are the
only numbers in the figure pipeline that do not come from results/sweep.csv,
so they live in one file with their source attached rather than hardcoded in
a plotting script -- which is where they used to live, in
src/benchmarking_cube.py, alongside a hardcoded copy of our own results that
Values are radii D, not minimum pairwise distances (which are 2D).

EUCLIDEAN.label: Packomania
EUCLIDEAN.note: Packomania marks N = 1 and 3-10 as proven optimal (in bold on its page); the rest are best known.

EUCLIDEAN.label: Benchmark (Kazakov)
EUCLIDEAN.note: Not certified optima. At p = 1 the exact answer is the inradius of the unit regular tetrahedron, $1/(2 \cdot \sqrt{6}) = 0.20412415$, which this benchmark misses by 1.8%; the reported gap to it should be read with that in mind.
